decision: Which approach best resolves: WF-084 must decide how a federated sign-in establishes that a profile belongs to the expected tenant. The research says the app asserts profile.organizationId matches the expected tenant and only then creates a session, and that validating with an email domain is unsafe because an organization can allow addresses from outside its corporate domain. The research does not say what happens when the organization id in the profile matches the expected tenant but this app holds no record of that tenant.

state.change:
## What was built

A feature plugin for WF-084, federate staff SSO and auto-provision via SCIM, on prefix
/api/wf-084. It owns four domain modules and one feature module in the existing
security_governance package, two backend test files, and one frontend folder.

### The tenant assertion
The callback reads exactly one field from the profile, `organization_id`, and compares it to
the expected tenant. A profile from another organization is refused 403 with
reason=tenant_mismatch. A profile carrying no organization id is refused 403 with
reason=tenant_absent, even when its email is at the expected tenant's own domain. The email
is read only after the assertion has passed, for display and for the directory lookup.

### The authorization code
Ten minutes, quoted from the research. An expired code is refused 401 with
reason=authorization_code_expired and is never retried. An expired code and a foreign tenant
are two different statuses because they need two different remedies from a login surface.

### Directory Sync
A webhook with a per-directory token in a header, and the Events API as a pull through the
same reconciliation. Both carry the three SCIM operations the research names. A deprovision
soft-deletes the user, revokes every session the user holds, and reports how many it revoked.

### Groups and access
Groups map to roles. There is no route, no engine method and no stored field that grants a
person access by hand; a test walks the route table and asserts it.

## What was measured

- 198 backend tests in the two WF-084 files pass, each on its own and together.
- ruff check and ruff format --check pass across backend, tools and orchestration.
- The frontend suite passes at 751 tests in 28 files; lint reports 0 errors; prettier reports
  every file already formatted; the build succeeds and the page is in the bundle.
- python backend/seed.py prints this feature's line, and the string encodes as cp1252.
- tools/verify_all_routes.py against a live uvicorn: no route returned 5xx, across all 78
  features. WF-084's own 24 routes were then walked end to end over real HTTP.
- Coverage was measured with the whole suite under four-agent contention, so the number
  understates the truth. CI is the authority.

## Defects found and fixed during verification

Three bugs were found by the real-HTTP walkthrough after the domain tests were green, and
each is now covered by a named regression test:

1. A replayed Events API pull updated a soft-deleted directory user, and deleting an
   already-deleted row raised. A pull that worked once and failed the second time would stop
   applying directory changes on any tenant that polls.
2. A repeated deprovision returned a raw store id in a 404 body instead of completing.
3. The tenant assertion response could not carry the ten-minute bound, because one constant
   was doing duty as both a field name and a field value. Two live routes returned 500.

## The one decision a reviewer should look at

Jev was asked whether the callback should require that this app holds a record of the tenant
a profile names, rather than comparing the two ids alone. It chose
assert_and_require_a_tenant_record over assert_only and auto_create_the_tenant at
confidence 0.99, audit jev-20261004T181259-19372-79165. Asserting the ids alone would let any
provider the app trusts mint a session for a tenant nobody configured, and auto-creating the
tenant would turn the assertion into a no-op for an id nobody has seen.

    dsr/security_governance/sso_vocabulary.py                 100%
    dsr/security_governance/sso_inferences.py                 100%
    dsr/security_governance/sso_rules.py                       97%
    dsr/security_governance/sso_engine.py                       94%
    dsr/features/wf084_..._via_scim.py                          99%

  in any WF-084 file. prettier reports every file already formatted. The build succeeds and
  the descriptor is present in the emitted bundle.
- python backend/seed.py prints this feature's line and the string encodes as cp1252. A test
  prints it and asserts the encode, because one non-cp1252 character once broke the whole
  seeder.
- tools/verify_all_routes.py against a live uvicorn: no route returned 5xx, across all 78
  features. WF-084's own 24 routes were then walked end to end over real HTTP, 45 calls
  covering the happy path and every refusal.
- The whole backend suite is run separately for the project-wide coverage figure; it is slow
  locally because four agents share eight cores. CI is the authority for that number.

## The one decision a reviewer should look at

Jev was asked whether the callback should require that this app holds a record of the tenant
a profile names, rather than comparing the two ids alone. It chose
assert_and_require_a_tenant_record over assert_only and auto_create_the_tenant at
confidence 0.99, audit jev-20261004T181259-19372-79165. Asserting the ids alone would let any
provider the app trusts mint a session for a tenant nobody configured, and auto-creating the

## How each stated requirement is met, and where the test that proves it lives

| Requirement | Where it is proved |
|---|---|
| Assert the organization id, never the email domain | `assert_tenant` reads one field; a test asserts its signature cannot receive a domain, and one asserts a guest address at the expected tenant's domain is refused |
| A session only after the assertion | `complete_sign_in` asserts before it writes; tests assert a refused sign-in writes no session and no audit row |
| An expired code is refused, not retried | `code_state` against the quoted ten minutes; the callback raises 401 before anything else runs |
| Three identifiers, three jobs | `IDENTIFIER_JOBS`, asserted so exactly one flag is set per entry; `identifier_kind` reports which one arrived |
| Both entry points, one callback | the flow field is stored per session; tests assert an IdP-initiated session is asserted too and that its RelayState redirect URI is checked |
| Deprovisioning removes access | `_deprovision` revokes every session and soft-deletes; a test asserts `sessions_revoked == 1` and that the session reads dead afterwards |
| Groups inform access rules | `resolve_access` is the only access input; a test walks the route table and asserts no route grants a person access |
| The directory is the source of truth | no manual access field exists; a test asserts that on the engine's source text and on the route table |
| Both delivery paths | `apply_directory_event` and `poll_events` share the reconciliation; a test asserts one event produces one log row |
